title: 2 kWh Power Station for an RV (2026): The 30-Amp Plug Catch
short_title: Your power station's 30-amp RV plug isn't 30 amps
summary: A 2 kWh portable power station with a TT-30 (30-amp RV) outlet gives about 20 A, not 30 A. This video covers what that runs, two traps after you plug the RV in (the converter and a two-way fridge on AUTO), how long 2 kWh lasts in an RV, and how the BLUETTI AC200L, Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2, Renogy PowerStation 2000, BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 and Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 compare.
short_summary: A power station's TT-30 RV outlet gives about 20 A from a 2,400 W inverter, not 30 A. Plus two traps: the RV converter and a two-way fridge on AUTO.

long.say: Thinking of a two-kilowatt-hour power station for your RV? There are three things the spec sheets don't spell out, and one of them is the thirty-amp plug. Quick note: if you buy through the links in the description, Dealectric earns a commission, at no cost to you.

long.say: First: a TT-30 outlet on a power station does not give you thirty amps. A twenty-four-hundred-watt inverter tops out around twenty amps. That runs the RV fridge, the water pump, the lights and a coffee maker. It does not run the full thirty-amp service, and it runs the rooftop air conditioner for only about an hour.

slide.cap: is what a power station's TT-30 RV outlet gives, not 30 A
slide.note: A 2,400 W inverter runs the fridge, water pump, lights and a coffee maker, not the full 30 A service

long.say: Second: once you plug the RV into the station, the RV's converter charges its house battery from it, at up to about eight hundred watts. Switch the converter off once that battery is full. Third: set a two-way fridge to propane. On auto, it draws two point four to three point six kilowatt-hours a day, which is more than the whole pack.

long.say: Here's the field. The BLUETTI AC200L, Anker's SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 and the Renogy PowerStation 2000 all have a built-in RV outlet and a twenty-four-hundred-watt inverter. The AC200L and the Renogy take up to twelve hundred watts of solar. Anker's is the lightest, at about forty-two pounds; the AC200L is the heaviest, at about sixty-two. BLUETTI's Elite 200 V2 has no RV outlet, so it needs an adapter, but it's rated for six thousand cycles, twice the AC200L. Jackery's 2000 v2 has no RV outlet and takes only four hundred watts of solar.

slide.foot: Specs from each maker's US page, read 2026-10-31

long.say: How long does it last? A twelve-volt compressor fridge uses about point seven kilowatt-hours a day, a furnace blower point three to point five on a cold night, and lights, phones and the water pump about point two. That's roughly one point two to one point five a day: about a day and a half with no sun, and two to three days with two to four hundred watts of solar.

slide.note: About 1.5 days with no sun; 2–3 days with 200–400 W of solar

long.say: To recharge: a campground outlet fills it in about an hour to an hour and a half. A DC-to-DC alternator charger adds five hundred sixty to eight hundred watts while you drive, while the twelve-volt socket gives only about a hundred. And four hundred watts of solar puts back one to one and a half kilowatt-hours on a good day.

items: 560–800 W while driving (the 12 V socket: ~100 W)

short.say: That thirty-amp RV outlet on your power station? It isn't thirty amps.

short.say: A twenty-four-hundred-watt inverter tops out around twenty amps. Enough for the fridge, the water pump, the lights and a coffee maker. Not the rooftop AC for more than about an hour.
Two more traps. Switch the RV's converter off, or it drains the station into the house battery. And set a two-way fridge to propane: on auto it can use more than the whole pack in a day.
